nodes.label: Backend Engineer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: APIs are the contracts between agent domains, so they must be precise and resilient; there is no human fallback to patch a broken contract.

nodes.label: Data Engineer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Bad schema decisions compound over time; migrations are treated as one-way because rollback of a data migration is unsafe.

nodes.label: DevOps Engineer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: The deployment pipeline must operate without human approval gates while keeping safety, so every manual step is treated as a bug.

nodes.label: Security Engineer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Security controls must be automated and self-enforcing; assume breach and isolate agents from the credentials of other agents.

nodes.label: Partial Failure Handling
nodes.rationale: Timeouts, retries with backoff, and circuit breakers keep one failing service from cascading.

nodes.label: Idempotent Operation Requirement
nodes.rationale: Retries must be safe because autonomous agents retry automatically without human judgement.

nodes.label: Inline Data Quality Checks
nodes.rationale: Quality checks run on every pipeline execution rather than as a separate job so bad data never lands silently.

nodes.label: ETL Pipeline Patterns (Batch/Micro-batch/Streaming/CDC)
nodes.rationale: Pattern choice is driven by required latency versus complexity and load on the source system.

nodes.label: Zero-Downtime Migration Strategy
nodes.rationale: Add nullable column, dual-write, backfill, switch reads, then drop the old column in a separate deploy - schema and code changes never ship together.

nodes.label: Schema Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Timestamp columns, UUID primary keys, and enforced foreign keys make schemas self-documenting for distributed systems.

nodes.label: Tested Rollback Path
nodes.rationale: Every deploy must have a tested rollback because an autonomous pipeline has no human to improvise recovery.

nodes.label: Runtime Secret Injection
nodes.rationale: Secrets are injected at runtime, never baked into images or committed, so an image leak is not a credential leak.

nodes.label: Immutable Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Every privileged action is logged immutably to make repudiation impossible.

nodes.label: Least Privilege Principle
nodes.rationale: Minimum permissions, exposure, and data retention limit blast radius when a component is compromised.

nodes.label: Incident Response Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Detect, triage, mitigate, resolve, post-incident - stop the bleeding before fixing root cause.

nodes.label: VITE_AUTH_ENABLED false Offline Mode
nodes.rationale: Falls back to an X-Company-Id header instead of a session; only valid against an API started with AUTH_ENABLED false and explicitly never for deployment.

nodes.label: httpOnly Cookie Session Authentication
nodes.rationale: The session lives in an httpOnly cookie so JavaScript cannot read the token; every request sends credentials include.

nodes.label: Cross-Origin Credential Allowlist Requirement
nodes.rationale: Pointing VITE_API_BASE_URL straight at the API bypasses the proxy, so that origin must appear in the backend cors_origins allowlist - cookies only travel cross-origin with credentials plus an explicit allow.

nodes.label: X-CSRF-Token Double-Submit Protection
nodes.rationale: Mutations carry X-CSRF-Token read back from the nv_csrf cookie, the standard defense once auth moves to cookies.

nodes.label: Dashboard Design System
nodes.rationale: Indigo primary, Emerald success, Amber warning, Rose danger, 8px spacing grid, Tailwind utility classes.

nodes.label: RequireAuth Route Guard
nodes.rationale: Wraps routes and redirects signed-out visitors to /login, or to /setup on a fresh install where the first administrator is created.

nodes.label: Dashboard Route Table
nodes.rationale: Routes spanning auth (/login, /setup, /invite) and operations (/agents, /tasks, /approvals, /budgets, /evolution, /workflows, /meetings, /activity, /settings).

nodes.label: Dashboard Technology Stack
nodes.rationale: React 19, TypeScript 5, Vite 6, Tailwind 4, React Router v7, Recharts, Lucide React.

nodes.label: Dashboard HTML Entry Point
nodes.rationale: Dark-mode-by-default shell mounting the root div and loading /src/main.tsx as an ES module; preconnects Google Fonts for IBM Plex Mono, Inter, and Space Grotesk.

nodes.label: NEXUS Dashboard Application
nodes.rationale: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind SPA giving real-time visibility into agents, tasks, budgets, workflows, and organizational evolution.

nodes.label: Secure Code Review Focus Areas
nodes.rationale: Auth boundaries, input trust, secret handling, error verbosity, dependency CVEs, and agent permission escalation.

nodes.label: Software Architect Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Prefer reversible decisions over optimal ones because the company evolves rapidly; bounded contexts align with agent boundaries.

nodes.label: Architecture Design Document Template
nodes.rationale: Standard sections (system overview, Mermaid component diagram, data-flow sequence, API boundary table, technology choices with reasons) so architecture output is comparable across agents.

nodes.label: Deployment Strategies (Rolling/Blue-Green/Canary/Recreate)
nodes.rationale: Each strategy trades resource cost against rollback speed; Recreate is only acceptable when downtime is.

nodes.label: Architecture Decision Records
nodes.rationale: Documenting decisions, not just designs, preserves the why for agents that arrive later.

nodes.label: Reversible Decision Preference
nodes.rationale: The company evolves rapidly, so a reversible decision beats a theoretically optimal irreversible one.

nodes.label: Explicit Trade-off Matrix
nodes.rationale: At least two viable options are compared so other agents can reason about what was given up.

nodes.label: Error Budget Feature Freeze
nodes.rationale: When the budget is burned, features freeze and reliability work is prioritized - the budget is a real control, not advice.

nodes.label: Data Fetching Hooks (useApi/usePolling/useAgents)
nodes.rationale: Standardized loading and error state handling instead of per-component fetch logic.

nodes.label: 30-Second Auto-Refresh Polling
nodes.rationale: The dashboard polls every 30 seconds, configurable in Settings.

nodes.label: Dashboard Source Layout
nodes.rationale: src/api, components split by domain (activity, agents, charts, common, evolution, governance, layout, org, tasks), hooks, pages, types, utils.

nodes.label: Frontend Engineer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Dashboards are the primary window into system health and agent activity; stale data in an autonomous system is dangerous.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.1 AA Accessibility Requirement
nodes.rationale: Accessibility is treated as a hard constraint, not a later audit item.

nodes.label: Atomic Component Architecture
nodes.rationale: Atoms-to-pages layering keeps each component single-responsibility with a clear props interface.

nodes.label: Loading/Error/Empty State Requirement
nodes.rationale: Every data fetch has explicit states because a blank panel in an ops dashboard is indistinguishable from a healthy one.

nodes.label: Server vs Client State Separation
nodes.rationale: API data is cached and invalidated separately from UI state; the URL is the source of truth for shareable views.

nodes.label: Product Manager Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Product decisions must be data-driven and hypothesis-based because there is no human intuition to fall back on.

nodes.label: PRD Work-Product Template
nodes.rationale: Problem, user stories, success metrics, technical requirements, constraints, dependencies, and explicit out-of-scope - forces scope boundaries to be written down.

nodes.label: One Metric Per Feature Rule
nodes.rationale: If it cannot be measured it cannot be learned from, so each feature carries exactly one success metric.

nodes.label: PRD Template (Problem/Hypothesis/Metrics/Scope)
nodes.rationale: Framing work as a testable hypothesis with one primary metric plus guardrails makes outcomes measurable.

nodes.label: Golden Signals (Latency/Traffic/Errors/Saturation)
nodes.rationale: Four signals cover most failure modes without requiring the question to be anticipated.

nodes.label: Code Reviewer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Code review is a critical quality gate in an autonomous company because no human reviews the diff before merge.

nodes.label: QA Engineer Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Quality gates must be automated and thorough since there is no manual testing phase.

nodes.label: Review Priority Markers (Blocker/Suggestion/Nit)
nodes.rationale: Severity tiers let an autonomous reviewer make an explicit approve-or-block decision instead of drip-feeding comments.

nodes.label: RICE Prioritization Framework
nodes.rationale: Reach times Impact times Confidence divided by Effort forces an explicit numeric trade-off instead of intuition.

nodes.label: Systematic Edge Case Generation
nodes.rationale: Empty, boundary, invalid-type, malicious, concurrent, and state-transition inputs are enumerated for every input.

nodes.label: Flaky Tests Are Bugs
nodes.rationale: Fix or delete, never skip - a skipped test silently removes a quality gate.

nodes.label: Regression Test Before Fix (Red then Green)
nodes.norm_label: regression test before fix (red then green)
nodes.rationale: Writing the failing test first proves the bug is understood and prevents recurrence.

nodes.label: STRIDE Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information Disclosure, DoS, Elevation of Privilege - a checklist over attack surfaces.

nodes.label: SRE Agent Role
nodes.rationale: Reliability is a feature with a measurable budget; error budgets fund velocity, so reliability work must reference an SLO.

nodes.label: Ten-Stage CI/CD Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Fail fast on cheap checks (lint, unit) before expensive ones (integration, staging) so feedback is quick.

nodes.label: LCP Under 2.5s Performance Budget
nodes.rationale: A measurable budget turns performance into a pass/fail gate rather than a preference.

nodes.label: Test Pyramid (Unit/Integration/E2E)
nodes.rationale: Many cheap unit tests, fewer expensive end-to-end tests, because E2E maintenance cost scales badly.

nodes.label: Chaos Engineering Practice
nodes.rationale: Failures are injected regularly to verify that resilience and response procedures actually work.

nodes.label: SLO and Error Budget Framework
nodes.rationale: SLIs as good-over-total ratios, targets from user expectations, error budget is 100 percent minus the target over a rolling window.

nodes.label: Toil Automation Rule
nodes.rationale: Anything done manually twice is automated the third time.

nodes.label: API Base URL and Dev Proxy
nodes.norm_label: api base url and dev proxy
nodes.rationale: An empty VITE_API_BASE_URL means same-origin through the mock dev server; PROXY_API true forwards every /api/* call to the real backend.

nodes.label: Central API Client (src/api/client.ts)
nodes.rationale: All API calls funnel through one module handling base URL, error normalization, and JSON parsing.

nodes.label: REST API Design Principles
nodes.rationale: Consistent plural-noun resources, cursor-based pagination, and Pydantic-validated schemas keep agent-to-agent contracts predictable.

nodes.label: Agent Credential Isolation
nodes.rationale: No agent may reach the credentials or data of another agent, so one compromised agent is not a full compromise.

nodes.label: Bounded Context Per Agent
nodes.rationale: One agent, one clear domain - bounded contexts are aligned with agent boundaries.
